topic.title: Graph Robustness, Privacy, and Trustworthy Learning
topic.overview: Graph models depend on relationships as well as node attributes, creating distinctive vulnerabilities. Small edge changes can disrupt predictions, while model outputs can reveal sensitive links. This topic studies defenses, robustness evaluation, uncertainty, and ownership protection, with attention to how information propagates through relational structure.
topic.whyItMatters: Protecting a graph predictor requires specifying what an adversary can observe or modify. Average attack success can conceal severe exposure of a few important relationships, and a defense based on neighbor similarity must account for graphs where connected nodes legitimately differ. Evaluation needs to match these structural assumptions.
topic.evolution: Early representatives analyze prediction on weighted graphs and trust leakage. GNNGuard in 2020 reweights and prunes connections using relationships between features and structure. Later benchmarks reassess defenses at scale; a 2026 link-stealing study emphasizes success under very low false-positive rates, showing why average privacy metrics can miss concentrated vulnerabilities.
openQuestions: How can robustness defenses preserve informative connections between dissimilar nodes?
Which evaluations capture privacy risks concentrated in a small set of sensitive links?
